transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Erin Wallace (Mulberry Soft Head of Platform), Samir Desai (DevOps), Priya Kapoor (Security), Tommy Reed (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick ops-runbook and VPC readiness check before we flip the staging pilot. Discussed KMS integration, audit logs, and latency SLOs.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, Maya's CSM, Diego is the SE who will walk through the ops playbook items. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Erin: Good, thanks. We just came out of a sprint demo, so apologies if we're a touch late.
[00:12] Samir: All good. Got a list of network folks here, we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:16] Jordan: Perfect. Goal for today: validate network prerequisites for Redwood Private in your VPC, align on runbook ownership, and lock a pilot smoke window.
[00:25] Maya: Also to confirm security must-haves — KMS, audit logs, SSO.
[00:29] Diego: I'll share screen in a sec, but just to set context: our ops-playbook outlines peering steps, IP ranges, firewall egress rules, and a sample smoke test. We want to make sure your infra team sees the exact checks.
[00:44] Erin: Sounds great. Our main driver is predictable latency for search features; cost is secondary but still in scope. We want to avoid a big lift on your end but ensure the compliance boxes are checked.
[00:55] Jordan: Understood. Tommy, from an exec perspective, what are the must-haves for a successful pilot?
[01:01] Tommy: Minimal user-facing regressions, sub-200ms P95 on our core generation path, and zero data leakage — particularly for customer PII. If we hit those, we can move to a paid pilot.
[01:12] Jordan: That's helpful — P95 target noted.
[01:15] Diego: Ok, jumping to slide 2 — network topology. Redwood Private runs inside your VPC with a control plane that may be customer-managed or hosted depending on the package. For you we recommended customer-managed control plane with private peering.
[01:29] Samir: Quick clar — when you say peering, do we need a full VPC peering or just a transit gateway route? We prefer using our TGW.
[01:37] Diego: TGW is totally fine. We just need bi-directional routing for the agent subnets and the NAT egress for model downloads. The playbook has both the peering and TGW options.
[01:47] Priya: On encryption — we need KMS integration for in-flight and at-rest keys. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and HSM rotation?
[01:56] Diego: Yes, Redwood Private supports external KMS providers; we have documented the API hooks. Rotations are supported but we'll need the key metadata and IAM role to set up automated sync.
[02:08] Erin: Can you clarify audit logging? Our security team requires immutable audit logs for token usage and model access with 90-day retention.
[02:15] Maya: We can route audit logs to your CloudWatch/S3 via our ingestion connector. Retention policies live on your side, so 90 days is fine. We'll show the exact ARN permissions.
[02:24] Samir: Any special firewall ports to open?
[02:27] Diego: Mostly outbound to our model repo endpoints (443) and to the control plane management IPs on 443. The playbook lists the CIDR blocks, but note they can be IPs that change during upgrades — we recommend naming the FQDNs rather than hardcoding IPs.
[02:42] [Speaker 2]: There's a note about internal KV cache traffic — if you plan to use multi-AZ cache you may want lower latency peering between your app subnets and the Redwood agents.
[02:53] Samir: Right, we are interested in multi-AZ for resilience, but cost is a concern. Is there a delta we can expect?
[03:00] Diego: Multi-AZ will add network egress and more agent nodes so cost rises, but it cuts P99 tail latency. We can provide an estimate once we see your token/seq length distribution.
[03:11] Priya: About data residency — we host in US-East; is there an option to pin regions?
[03:16] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private can be constrained to specific regions. For Mulberry we proposed US-East due to your user base. If you need EU data locality later, we can separate deployments.
[03:26] Erin: Timeline question — we want staging smoke tests within two weeks, and production ramp within six weeks if all good. Feasible?
[03:34] Maya: That timeline is aggressive but doable. We need the VPC peering done and smoke test window scheduled.
[03:40] Diego: Also need the KMS info and a short test dataset with synthetic PII redaction so we can validate audit logging.
[03:47] Samir: We'll run network checks today and Samir will upload the traceroute.
[03:52] Jordan: Great — let's talk SLAs. The dedicated recommendation includes latency SLOs. For Private we'll agree internal SLOs — the commercial contract will reflect those.
[04:01] Tommy: Wanted to flag regulatory — we may need SOC 2 attestation and client-specific audit cooperation later. Do you have artifacts?
[04:09] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II docs and an audit pack. We'll share redacted reports and the compliance runbook.
[04:15] Priya: On SSO — we use SAML-based IdP for admin roles; how is RBAC handled?
[04:21] Diego: RBAC maps to your IdP groups; we support SAML/SCIM provisioning. We'll need an admin user to test provisioning flows.
[04:29] [00:04:40] Erin: Who's owning the runbook on your side?
[04:43] Maya: I'll own post-deployment runbook iterations and handoff to your ops. Diego will maintain the technical doc.
[04:49] Diego: I'll drop the initial ops-playbook link into the ticket after the call.
[04:55] Jordan: Ok let's surface any blockers — Samir?
[04:58] Samir: Firewall rules are sometimes a bottleneck; also our infra team wants more precise IPs rather than ranges. You said FQDNs are better but security prefers pinned IPs. We might need a short-lived list for the pilot.
[05:09] Diego: We can provide a signed list for the pilot and then move to FQDNs for long-term.
[05:14] Priya: Another blocker: KMS vendor — we use HashiCorp Vault as KMS in our stack and need to ensure Redwood can talk to it via private endpoint.
[05:23] Diego: Vault is supported via our KMS adapter for customer-managed providers — just need the endpoint and auth method. We'll run a test together.
[05:31] [00:06:00] Jordan: Quick check — any concerns about model updates or rollback behavior during pilot?
[05:36] Diego: Rollbacks are supported; we keep model artifacts in a versioned registry. For Private we'll coordinate the update window with your maintenance window.
[05:44] Erin: Sounds good. Can we have a quick note on monitoring and alerting? We want CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and error budgets surfaced.
[05:53] Maya: Console provides per-route metrics and token-level cost breakdowns. We can set up basic alerts to your PagerDuty.
[05:58] Samir: Are there prebuilt dashboards?
[06:01] Diego: Yes, Grafana dashboards we provide out-of-the-box; we can push a dashboard JSON for your team to import.
[06:08] [00:06:30] Tommy: Pricing — are we still on the usage plus a private deployment fee? Need to confirm billing cadence.
[06:16] Jordan: Yes, for Private it's base platform fee + usage tier. I'll send the commercial summary after this call to the procurement contact.
[06:24] Priya: Any legal/contract blockers we should know about? Data processing addendum?
[06:29] Maya: We have a standard DPA and can add clauses for data residency and audit cooperation. Legal review usually takes 2–3 weeks.
[06:36] Erin: Ok, let's drill into the actual steps for the staging pilot.
[06:40] Diego: Pilot steps: 1) infra readiness (network, KMS, IAM) 2) deploy Redwood agents in staging 3) run smoke tests and synthetic workloads 4) measure latency and error rates 5) iterate.
[06:52] Jordan: Who from Mulberry will be the day-to-day contact for the pilot?
[06:56] Erin: Samir will be the primary; Priya for security sign-off. Tommy will be the exec sponsor.
[07:02] [00:07:10] Samir: We'll run the connectivity check today. Which traceroute info do you need?
[07:07] Diego: The usual—source and dest IPs, latency histogram, any packet drops. We'll have a small script we can send that runs the checks and uploads to a shared bucket.
[07:18] Maya: I'll put that script in the workspace and tag Samir.
[07:21] Samir: Great.
[07:23] Diego: Also note, for the multi-AZ KV cache we should align on sharding keys—this will impact latency and memory footprint.
[07:31] Erin: We probably won't start with multi-AZ; let's keep single AZ for staging.
[07:35] Diego: That's fine.
[07:36] Jordan: Anything else on security?
[07:38] Priya: One ask — do you have a runbook template for incident triage that includes steps for data-exfil suspicion? We need that before pilot.
[07:47] Maya: Yes, we have an incident triage template. I'll attach it to the ops-playbook doc bundle.
[07:52] [00:08:00] Jordan: Okay, I'm going to recap next steps: Diego will send ops-playbook v1 and the connectivity script; Samir will run network tests and upload outputs by 9/10; Priya will confirm KMS compatibility and key rotation policy by 9/11; Maya will schedule pilot smoke slot and send invites. Any additions?
[08:14] Erin: Could we add a short acceptance checklist for the pilot to the doc? E.g., P95 under threshold, audit logs validated, RBAC tested?
[08:22] Diego: Yes — we'll add an acceptance checklist to the playbook.
[08:25] Jordan: I'll also include a commercial summary and a timeline that mirrors our discussion.
[08:29] [00:08:36] Tommy: One small ask — can Redwood provide a short walkthrough for our SREs on day 1 of the pilot? 30–45 minutes?
[08:37] Maya: Absolutely, Diego and I can run a 45-minute runbook walkthrough on the pilot start day.
[08:43] Samir: that'll help.
[08:44] Priya: Also we'll need a dry run for SCIM provisioning — can we do that during the walkthrough?
[08:50] Diego: Yes, we can test SCIM and SAML provisioning in the walkthrough. Bring an admin test account.
[08:56] [00:09:15] Jordan: Any final Qs?
[09:00] Erin: No, sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone.
[09:03] Jordan: Thanks for the time. We'll follow up with the doc bundle and action items.
[09:08] Maya: I'll send the calendar invites and attach the playbook link.
[09:11] Diego: Dropping the first draft ops-playbook in the ticket right after.
[09:15] Samir: We'll try to have the traceroute by EOD.
[09:19] [00:09:40] Close: Call ended; recording saved.

Notes and references:
- Ops playbook (draft link): https://redwood.example.com/playbooks/mulberry-ops-v1 (placeholder link)
- Connectivity script: will be shared in ticket #12345
- Compliance docs: SOC2 redacted pack to be shared via secure link

End of transcript.
